why: Whether a node is balanced depends only on the sizes of its children's subtrees, which are computed bottom-up: size(v) = 1 + sum of children's sizes. One post-order pass gives every size and lets you check each node.
hints: You need the size of every subtree. Can a node's size be computed from its children's sizes?
Post-order: size(v) = 1 + sum(size(c)). A node is balanced if all its children's sizes are equal (trivially true with 0 or 1 child).
Get a parent-before-child order with an iterative DFS from 0, then process it in reverse to fill sizes and count. O(n) time and space.
pitfalls: Leaves and single-child nodes are balanced.
Deep chains break recursive DFS in Python; go iterative.
